title: SANEval: Open-Vocabulary Compositional Benchmarks with Failure-mode Diagnosis
claim: A modular evaluation pipeline parses prompts, detects objects, and routes outputs to separate scorers that return scores plus diagnostic feedback.
layout: Single panel, left-to-right flow, color-coded arrows routing to three stacked evaluators
description: A left-to-right block diagram. On the left, a legend and three colored prompt boxes (pink for attribute, purple for spatial, teal for numeracy), e.g. "A blue bench and a green bowl". Arrows lead to a yellow Prompt Understanding module and a green T2I generator. The generator produces example photos of benches and bowls, with borders matching the prompt colors. Those images feed a blue Enhanced Object Detection box. Blue arrows carry parsed JSON outputs (attributes, relations, counts) from the parser. Orange arrows carry images. Magenta arrows carry bounding boxes. All of these converge on three large rounded evaluation boxes, in pink, purple and teal: Attribute Binding, Spatial and Numeracy Evaluation. Each box has labeled inputs and outputs a score and Feedback arrow on the right.
caption: Block diagram of the SANEval benchmark.
abstract: Text-to-image (T2I) models struggle with compositional prompts requiring multiple objects, bound attributes, accurate counts, or spatial relations. Existing benchmarks face limits from fixed detector vocabularies, aggregated scores, and varying human-validation protocols. We introduce SANEval (Spatial, Attribute, and Numeracy Evaluation), an open-vocabulary compositional benchmark with two key contributions: (i) a public dataset of ~5,250 prompts paired with images from six state-of-the-art T2I models, split into algorithmically generated Simple and fully human-written Hard partitions across five compositional tasks, and (ii) a modular evaluation pipeline combining an LLM prompt parser, an open-vocabulary detector with LLM synonym expansion, and scorers for attribute binding, spatial relations, and numeracy. Each scorer emits numerical scores and diagnostic feedback for missing, extra, or mis-bound elements. Validated against human ratings (n = 500), SANEval achieves positive Pearson correlations across all categories (overall r = 0.222), outperforming CompBench++ (-0.016) and GenEval (-0.030). A manual audit of 24,012 detections shows 96.58% precision, with ablation confirming that synonym expansion is critical to pipeline performance. Dataset: [https://huggingface.co/datasets/saneval/saneval-release](https://huggingface.co/datasets/saneval/saneval-release). Pipeline: [https://github.com/nielseni6/saneval](https://github.com/nielseni6/saneval).
